processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Alloy ingots with nominal composition Fe-35Mn-17Al-5Cu (at.%) produced by vacuum induction melting of >99.9% pure raw materials under argon; ingots homogenized at 1200 °C for 24 h.

processing_steps.reduction_ratio: hot-rolled into plates with a thickness of 4 mm
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Homogenized ingots hot-rolled into plates 4 mm thick.
Plates cut into 10 × 5 × 2 mm3 samples for Vickers hardness measurements and microstructure characterizations.
Solution treated at 1100 °C for 10 min under an argon atmosphere, followed by oil quenching (parent process proc_st-1100c-10min-oq; solution-treated 17Al hardness = 259.8 ± 1.5 HV).
Solution-treated 17Al samples aged at 600 °C for 3 h, followed by water quenching. This defines the terminal state of the sample (17Al 600 °C/3 h).

structures.overall_structure: After aging the 17Al alloy at 600 °C for 3 h, the α (BCC) matrix has almost completely transformed into β-Mn; the SE-SEM image for this condition (Fig. 8, 600 °C-3 h panel) shows a uniform grey β-Mn matrix with no resolvable second phase at the 50 µm scale.

precipitates.distribution: within the β-Mn / at β-Mn interfaces

structures.overall_structure: Solution-treated Fe-Mn-Al-Cu low-density steels (including the 17Al alloy) consist of a single α (BCC) phase; the 17Al EBSD phase map is uniformly α (BCC).

interfaces.phase_evolution: α → α + FCC Cu-rich phase → α-Mn + β-Mn + BCC phase → β-Mn + BCC phase + FCC Cu-rich phase
interfaces.interface_notes: For the 17Al alloy at 600 °C/3 h the α→β-Mn transformation is essentially complete; the general sequence of microstructural evolution during aging of Fe-Mn-Al-Cu low-density steels is given in b0068. The 17Al interface micrographs (FCC Cu-rich particles at β-Mn interfaces, FCC twins) were documented by TEM on the hardest sample (575 °C/6 h), not directly on this 600 °C/3 h sample.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers microhardness tester HVS-1000, load 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times and averaged

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Load 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times, values averaged
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure the hardness of the 17Al alloy before and after aging to track the aging hardening behaviour
characterization_methods.key_findings: 17Al aged at 600 °C for 3 h: 794.6 ± 58.1 HV; solution-treated baseline: 259.8 ± 1.5 HV.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: ZEISS Sigma 300 SEM operated at 5 kV
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Polished surfaces; main panels 50 µm scale bar with higher-magnification insets
characterization_methods.purpose: Image the precipitation of secondary phases (α-Mn, β-Mn) and the transformed matrix in the 17Al alloy after different aging treatments (Fig. 8)
characterization_methods.key_findings: The 600 °C-3 h panel of the 17Al alloy (Fig. 8) shows a uniform grey β-Mn matrix, with no labels or inset, consistent with near-complete α→β-Mn transformation.

unmapped_findings: The 17Al alloy specific sample aged at 600 °C for 3 h is documented only by Vickers hardness (Table 3: 794.6 ± 58.1 HV) and one SE-SEM panel (Fig. 8, 600 °C-3 h, uniform grey β-Mn matrix); no EBSD, XRD or TEM characterization was performed directly on this exact 600 °C/3 h condition.

For the 17Al alloy the reported β-Mn intrinsic hardness (12.2 ± 0.1 GPa, nanoindentation) and β-Mn composition (Mn 36.2 at.%, Al 16.3 at.%, Cu 2.6 at.%; SEM-EDS) were measured on the hardest sample (575 °C/6 h, 924.9 HV), not on the 600 °C/3 h sample; the peak-hardness 17Al fracture toughness KIC = 6.6 MPa·m1/2 also refers to the 575 °C/6 h sample, so these values are not attributed to this sample.

Aging hardening response of Fe-Mn-Al-Cu low-density steels generally slows with increasing Al content; for the 17Al alloy the α→β-Mn transformation is essentially complete after 6 h at 550 °C but after only 1 h at 600 °C and above, consistent with the fully transformed β-Mn matrix observed for this 600 °C/3 h sample.
